arguments: {"summary": "Reviewed the 100-file plexus-utils snapshot (pom 3.0.16-SNAPSHOT). The strongest source-evidenced issue is a quote/escape bypass in the command-line building path: StringUtils.quoteAndEscape short-circuits and returns a caller-supplied string verbatim whenever it merely starts and ends with the quote delimiter, without escaping or neutralizing its contents. Shell.getRawCommandLine relies on that method to make arguments safe before Commandline.execute() passes the assembled string to sh -c / cmd /C via Runtime.exec, so an argument that is fully wrapped in the shell quote character (single quote on BourneShell, double quote on CmdShell/default Shell) is interpreted by the shell instead of being passed as a literal argument. This is one root cause (trusting pre-quoted input in the escaping helper) and therefore one candidate. Other plausible issues were considered and are listed as unconfirmed/rejected leads; no candidate was runtime-confirmed.", "candidates": [{"id": "cand-001", "title": "Shell argument escaping bypassed for already-quoted strings in StringUtils.quoteAndEscape (command injection)", "weakness_type": "CWE-78 OS Command Injection / CWE-116 Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output", "root_cause": "StringUtils.quoteAndEscape (src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/StringUtils.java:2314-2318) returns source unchanged when force is false and source startsWith and endsWith the quote character. The shortcut treats any string that merely begins and ends with the quote character as already-quoted-and-trusted, so the characters between the quotes are never escaped with the escape pattern nor wrapped by the quoting logic. Shell.getRawCommandLine (src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/cli/shell/Shell.java:145-167) calls this helper with force=false to build the single command string passed to the OS shell, so the bypass propagates directly to shell execution.", "locations": [{"path": "src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/StringUtils.java", "start_line": 2303, "end_line": 2349}, {"path": "src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/cli/shell/Shell.java", "start_line": 132, "end_line": 178}, {"path": "src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/cli/shell/BourneShell.java", "start_line": 55, "end_line": 69}, {"path": "src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/cli/Commandline.java", "start_line": 618, "end_line": 660}], "attacker_control": "Any string that an application passes as an argument to Commandline.createArg().setValue(...), Commandline.addArguments(...), or new Commandline(toProcess) and that an external/untrusted source can influence. The bypass is triggered by an argument whose first and last characters are the active quote delimiter: a single quote for the BourneShell used on Unix-like systems (BourneShell sets the argument quote delimiter to a single quote and a single-quote-wrapped escape pattern at BourneShell.java:55-69), or a double quote for the default Shell/CmdShell used on Windows. The interior text can then contain shell metacharacters (semicolon, ampersand, backticks, dollar-parenthesis, etc.) that the helper would normally have quoted or escaped.", "prerequisites": "The application must pass untrusted data as a whole argument to the plexus-utils Commandline/Shell API and then execute it (Commandline.execute() calls Runtime.getRuntime().exec(getShellCommandline(), env[, cwd]) at Commandline.java:636/651). The argument value must begin and end with the shell's quote delimiter. This is a library-level weakness: exploitability depends on a consuming application's argument plumbing, which cannot be enumerated from this snapshot.", "trace": "Commandline.addArguments/createArg stores raw argument strings (Commandline.java:341-425, 739-745) -> Shell.getShellCommandLine invokes getCommandLine -> Shell.getRawCommandLine iterates arguments and calls StringUtils.quoteAndEscape(arguments[i], getArgumentQuoteDelimiter(), escapeChars, getQuotingTriggerChars(), getArgumentEscapePattern(), false) (Shell.java:167) -> quoteAndEscape sees that source startsWith and endsWith the quote character and returns the raw argument unescaped (StringUtils.java:2314-2318) instead of reaching the escape/wrap logic (2320-2348) -> the raw text is concatenated into one command string -> Commandline.execute() runs it through sh -c / cmd.exe /C (Commandline.java:636/651), so embedded metacharacters are interpreted by the shell rather than delivered as a literal argument. The same helper is used by CommandLineUtils.toString(String[]) (CommandLineUtils.java:493-496), broadening exposure for callers that build shell strings from it.", "impact": "Arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the process that uses this utility library to launch a command with attacker-influenced arguments (confidentiality, integrity and availability impact). Because the bypass defeats the library's only argument-escaping step, a consuming application can reasonably believe the argument is safely quoted while the shell executes embedded commands.", "counterevidence_checked": "Verified that the bypass only fires when the string both starts and ends with the quote delimiter, so ordinary values without leading/trailing quotes are still escaped/quoted; force=true callers would not hit it, but Shell.getRawCommandLine passes false. Checked the surrounding escape logic (StringUtils.escape, 2358-2399) and BourneShell's single-quote-wrapped escape pattern; they correctly neutralize quote characters when they are reached, which strengthens the conclusion that the early return is the defect. Checked whether MXParser (the only XML parser in the tree) could resolve external entities for an XXE candidate: setFeature(FEATURE_PROCESS_DOCDECL, true) is explicitly rejected and parseDocdecl() only scans to the closing angle bracket, so no XXE lead was promoted. No runtime execution was performed; the trigger condition was established by reading the control flow only.", "confidence": "medium", "unverified": "Exploitability depends on a consuming application exposing untrusted data as a command argument, which is outside this snapshot; the exact historical fix/CVE mapping is not verifiable offline.
